story.title: Weather and water movement
story.lead: Weather agencies reported rain and atmospheric changes across the region [1]. Air and water masses move based on density differences [2].
stat.1.label: mass of the water or air sample
stat.2.label: volume of the sample space
stat.3.label: resulting density
story.body_1: When rain falls or air warms, masses shift and create weather patterns. Emergency teams monitor rainfall and issue advisories [1]. Understanding water and air helps communities stay prepared [3].
story.body_2: Knowing how mass spreads over a volume helps scientists predict storms and floods. Science keeps communities safe during extreme weather [1].
timeline.1.text: Air and moisture begin to shift.
timeline.2.text: Rain clouds form over the region.
physics.title: Mass, volume and density
physics.body_1: Density tells us how much mass is packed into a specific volume. A denser material has more mass in the same space.
physics.body_2: In physics, density equals mass divided by volume. This equation helps explain why objects float or sink in water.
physics.assumptions: We assume uniform composition throughout the sample.
table.note: Higher mass in the same volume increases density.
graph.title: Density under different sample masses
graph.1.label: Water
graph.2.label: Air
graph.3.label: Dense
graph.note: Density grows directly as mass increases on a constant volume.
physics.tip: Bigger mass in the same volume means higher density. Smaller volume with the same mass also raises density.
